decision: behavioral anchor = sugar/bitter feeding experiment (Shiu et al. 2024, Fig 3a)

why_sugar_bitter_is_sharper: Directional qualitative prediction on a fixed readout: bitter must DECREASE sugar-driven MN9 firing; a sign convention that breaks GABA/glutamate inhibition predicts the opposite (increase). The readout flips with the convention.
Both driven populations are primary sensory GRNs (cholinergic, directly Poisson-driven); no cross-dataset homology mapping of interneurons required.
Bitter GRNs' effect on MN9 is mediated by inhibitory interneurons - the prediction REQUIRES inhibition to survive in the circuit, which is exactly the assumption under test.
MN9 motor neurons verified present in male-cns:v0.9 (MN9_L 10331, MN9_R 16949).
why_grooming_is_weaker: Key manipulation silences three inhibitory neurons whose identity was model-derived; testing it requires identifying those same neurons in MaleCNS first (homology-mapping confound stacked on the sign question).
JON->grooming involves complex mechanosensory circuitry where a broken sign convention could still produce a plausible-looking result.

protocol_from_figures_ipynb_cells_23_25.sugar_grns: 21 labellar sugar-sensing GRNs (right hemisphere), FlyWire IDs in figures.ipynb cell 23
protocol_from_figures_ipynb_cells_23_25.bitter_grns: 20 labellar bitter-sensing GRNs (Gr66a class), FlyWire IDs in cell 23
protocol_from_figures_ipynb_cells_23_25.frequencies: sugar 0-180 Hz x bitter 0-200 Hz grid (cell 24)
protocol_from_figures_ipynb_cells_23_25.readout: MN9 (proboscis-extension motor neuron) firing rate (cell 25 -> fig_3a_rate.csv)
protocol_from_figures_ipynb_cells_23_25.expected_result: bitter suppresses sugar-driven MN9 firing (paper Fig 3a)

prerequisite: map FlyWire GRN IDs -> male-cns:v0.9 bodyIds (gustatory class, 1428 candidates; flywireType/matchingNotes fields available as mapping aids)
pass_criterion: MN9 rate under sugar+bitter < MN9 rate under sugar alone, reproducing the paper's directional finding
fail_criterion: MN9 rate under sugar+bitter >= sugar alone => NT-sign convention is falsified for this circuit (or GRN mapping is wrong - distinguish before concluding)
